request.system:
You classify one recorded call at Aegis Cloud Security, a B2B SaaS company, against a fixed theme taxonomy (version v1).

You receive the full transcript as numbered turns in the form "[index] Speaker (side): sentence". side is "customer" (works at an outside company) or "aegis_staff" (works at Aegis). You are given nothing else about the call: no title, no call type, no summary. Judge only from the words in the transcript.

THEMES (what kind of conversation it is; pick by what the call is mostly about):
1. Commercial Renewals and Retention: Renewals, contracts, pricing and SLA negotiation, churn risk, expansion deals. Boundary: If a call is mainly about product adoption with renewal as an aside, use Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion.
2. Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion: Previews, launches, early access, roadmap input, feature requests, adoption and compliance-readiness reviews of the product, and internal launch-readiness reviews. Boundary: The module belongs in the product area field, not in the theme. Renewal talk that is only an aside stays here.
3. Incident and Outage Response: War rooms, root cause, remediation plans, customer impact assessment, incident communication, postmortems, reliability reviews. Boundary: A single customer's technical fault that is not a platform incident belongs in Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
4. Technical Integration and Performance Issues: Support-style troubleshooting: SSO, SAML, SCIM, LDAP, MFA failures, connectors and SIEM integration, backup windows and throughput, report defects, API errors, internal scalability concerns. Boundary: Module-specific problems go here with the module in the product area field. A platform-wide outage is Incident and Outage Response.
5. Onboarding and Implementation Scoping: Kickoffs, deployment planning, architecture scoping, setup workshops. Boundary: Troubleshooting of an already deployed integration is Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
6. Billing and Usage Disputes: Invoices, overages, seat counts, billing adjustments. Boundary: Small theme (about 4 calls in the pilot); kept because it is distinct and actionable.
7. Competitive Strategy and Win/Loss: Competitive intelligence, battlecards, win/loss analysis, and customer-facing calls where the customer is evaluating alternatives. Boundary: Definition widened from the pilot's internal-only version to include customer calls about evaluating alternatives.
8. Internal Planning and Delivery Cadence: Standups, sprint planning, retros, all-hands, design and roadmap syncs with no customer or incident focus. Boundary: If a meeting is mainly an incident, use Incident and Outage Response.

Other / new theme: use only if no theme above fits. Then describe the call in one sentence in other_description. Other / new theme only if no theme fits. More than 10% of calls in Other triggers a taxonomy revision (new version, full re-run).

PRODUCT AREA (which module the call is about; exactly one):
- Detect: Threat detection, event ingestion, alerting.
- Comply: Compliance reporting and evidence mapping (including Comply v2).
- Protect: Backup, snapshots, disaster recovery (includes backup).
- Identity: Directory sync, SSO, SAML, SCIM, MFA, IAM governance.
- Platform/General: No single product dominates, or the call is cross-product.

INCIDENT: Set incident to '2026-03-detect-outage' (otherwise null) when the call's main purpose, or a major part of it, is the March 2026 Detect event-processing pipeline outage: cause, impact, remediation, customer communication or aftermath. A separate field so the outage story is visible across support, external and internal calls.

Return one record with:
- primary_theme: exactly one theme name copied from the list above, or "Other / new theme".
- tags: zero, one or two further theme names from the list that also clearly come up. Never repeat the primary theme. Empty when primary_theme is "Other / new theme".
- product_area: exactly one product area name copied from the list.
- incident: "2026-03-detect-outage" or null.
- other_description: one sentence if primary_theme is "Other / new theme", otherwise an empty string.
- evidence_quote: a short passage of at most 30 words that best supports primary_theme, copied EXACTLY, character for character, from the sentence part of ONE turn. Copy only the words after "Speaker (side): ". Never include the index, the speaker name, the side or the colon prefix. Do not paraphrase, do not shorten with "...", do not join text from different turns.
- confidence: "high" if clearly about the primary theme, "medium" if two themes compete, "low" if it fits poorly.
- taxonomy_version: "v1".

Return only JSON matching the schema.

[3] Marcus Williams (aegis_staff): Absolutely, totally understand, let's dive right in — so from the case notes it looks like you're seeing an issue with SAML certificate rotation in Aegis Identity, can you walk us through what you're experiencing?
[4] Vanessa Cruz (customer): Sure, so — we rotated our SAML signing certificate yesterday, standard procedure, we do this every six months, and after the rotation a significant portion of our users are getting authentication failures when they try to SSO into our internal tools.
[5] Elena Vasquez (aegis_staff): Okay and when you say a significant portion, are we talking like a handful of users or is this more widespread?
[6] Vanessa Cruz (customer): We're talking roughly sixty to seventy percent of our workforce right now, Elena, so — yeah, it's pretty bad, people can't get into Salesforce, they can't get into our inventory management system, it's basically grinding our retail ops team to a halt on a Sunday which is one of our busiest days.
[7] Marcus Williams (aegis_staff): Okay that's — yeah that's definitely a critical impact situation, I'm sorry you're dealing with that on a Sunday.
[8] Vanessa Cruz (customer): I mean, it shouldn't matter what day it is, this shouldn't be happening at all, right? We followed the documentation for certificate rotation step by step and now our people can't log in.
[9] Elena Vasquez (aegis_staff): You're right, you're absolutely right, and I want to dig into this because I actually have a hypothesis about what might be happening here — Vanessa, when you did the rotation, did you use the in-platform certificate wizard or did you upload the certificate manually through the admin console?
[10] Vanessa Cruz (customer): We used the wizard, the one that's supposed to handle the, uh, the propagation automatically, that's kind of the whole point of using it.
[11] Elena Vasquez (aegis_staff): Right, okay, so — I need to be transparent with you here Vanessa, we are aware of a bug that was introduced in the 3.4.1 release of Aegis Identity, and it specifically affects the certificate rotation wizard.
[12] Vanessa Cruz (customer): There's a bug.
[13] Elena Vasquez (aegis_staff): Yes, and — I want to explain what it's doing because it helps with the workaround — so essentially what's happening is the wizard is completing the cert rotation on the identity provider side but it's not properly propagating the new certificate metadata to all of the service provider connections, so some of your SP integrations are still trying to validate assertions against the old certificate.
[14] Vanessa Cruz (customer): So the wizard is broken. The tool that's supposed to make this safe and easy — is broken.
[15] Elena Vasquez (aegis_staff): I — yes, there's a defect in it, I'm not going to sugarcoat that, and I understand why that's incredibly frustrating especially given the impact you're seeing right now.
[16] Vanessa Cruz (customer): And this is — okay, sorry Marcus, I'm just — I'm really struggling here because we've been on this platform for two and a half years and we've had a rough few weeks, you guys had that Detect outage earlier this month and now this, it's like—
[17] Marcus Williams (aegis_staff): I hear you, I hear you completely and those are both legitimate concerns, but right now let's focus on getting your people back in, can we do that? Because I do have a path to resolution.
[18] Vanessa Cruz (customer): Yes, okay, yes please — what do we need to do.
[19] Elena Vasquez (aegis_staff): Okay so the fix is — it's a bit manual but it works, what you'll need to do is go into each service provider connection in the admin console and manually re-import the new certificate metadata for each integration, it won't be automatic through the wizard but once you do it per-SP the authentication will work correctly.
[20] Vanessa Cruz (customer): How many SP connections are we talking about, like, do you know how many integrations we have configured?
[21] Marcus Williams (aegis_staff): I'm pulling up your account right now — it looks like you have fourteen service provider connections active.
[22] Vanessa Cruz (customer): Fourteen. Okay so we have to manually touch fourteen integrations to fix something that your wizard was supposed to handle automatically.
[23] Elena Vasquez (aegis_staff): Yes, and — I can stay on this call with you the entire time and walk you through each one if that's helpful, I don't want you to have to figure this out alone.
[24] Vanessa Cruz (customer): I'm going to need to pull in one of my engineers to actually do the clicking around in the console, give me two minutes.
[25] Marcus Williams (aegis_staff): Of course, take your time.
[26] Vanessa Cruz (customer): While we wait — Elena, do you know when a proper fix is going to be released for this? Like when is the patch coming?
[27] Elena Vasquez (aegis_staff): So our engineering team has the fix built, it's going through QA validation right now, current target is a patch release in the 3.4.2 update which is scheduled for the week of April 6th.
[28] Vanessa Cruz (customer): April 6th. So for anyone who does a cert rotation before then they're going to hit this same problem.
[29] Elena Vasquez (aegis_staff): That's correct, and we are — we have a customer advisory going out today actually, warning admins not to use the wizard until 3.4.2, I know that doesn't help you retroactively but we are trying to prevent other customers from hitting this.
[30] Vanessa Cruz (customer): Would have been nice to have that warning before I ran the wizard yesterday.
[31] Elena Vasquez (aegis_staff): You're right, the advisory should have gone out sooner, I — I don't have a good answer for why it didn't and I'm not going to make excuses for that.
[32] Vanessa Cruz (customer): Okay, I have my engineer Priya on — she can go into the console, Elena can you walk us through the steps?
[33] Elena Vasquez (aegis_staff): Yes absolutely — Priya, if you go to the Aegis Identity admin console and navigate to Identity Federation, then Service Providers, you should see the list of all your SP connections there.
[34] Elena Vasquez (aegis_staff): And Vanessa, just so you know, Marcus and I are going to document everything from this call and I'm going to personally escalate this to our customer success team to make sure you get a proper follow-up on the overall reliability concerns you raised, the Detect outage, this bug — I want to make sure someone is having that bigger conversation with you.
[35] Vanessa Cruz (customer): I appreciate that, I do — I just, I need things to actually work, you know, we chose Aegis because we thought it was going to reduce our operational headaches not add to them.
[36] Marcus Williams (aegis_staff): That's fair, and that feedback is going to be heard, I promise you that — now let's get your team back online.
